opening.argument: The evidence presents straightforward earthquake reporting focused on emergency communication and information services. The report begins with the aftermath, explaining that “rescue teams are still looking for clues,” then describes Google’s platform for posting and searching for information about missing relatives, Facebook’s Safety Check-In feature, and Airtel’s offer of free calls to Nepal. The visuals reinforce that subject: one shows a Google Person Finder page for the 2015 Nepal Earthquake, and another shows a Nepal Earthquake page alongside Facebook Safety Check. These are reported response tools and public-interest updates, while the channel subscription language and channel-page imagery are ordinary audience engagement and publisher promotion separate from those services.

citations.quote: Seventy-two hours after a series of earthquakes shattered Nepal and parts of India, rescue teams are still looking for clues
Google has activated the Peoplegender platform which allows users to post and search for information about missing friends and relatives
While Facebook has started the Safety Check-In feature
